_note: Framework dimension -> DGIW pillar mappings.
coverageWeight is the share of THIS DIMENSION that THIS PILLAR accounts for.
Weights within a leaf dimension sum to 1.0 across the FULL entry set, including
banking-only entries. It is NOT 'how much of the pillar this dimension covers' —
under that reading a dimension score is not a weighted mean, the four scorecards
do not reconcile, and the decomposition back to pillar contributions is undefined.
LAYER and RETAINED SHARE. An entry is core, banking, or both. Under a layer filter
only the visible entries contribute, so a dimension carrying a banking-only entry
retains less than 1.0 under a core-only engagement — DM11 retains 0.85, DCAM7
retains 0.75. C2 renormalises the visible subset AND must print the retained share,
the same way scoring.ts prints confidence for a pillar. A dimension scored from 75%
of its declared mapping is not making the same claim as one scored from 100%.
No entry is core-only. That is deliberate, not an oversight: the banking overlay is
additive, so nothing in these frameworks is EXCLUDED from a banking engagement. The
same principle check-dgiw enforces as WAVE-LAYER.
Only leaf dimensions appear here. DIM-020/021/022 (DGI groups) and DIM-038 (COBIT
APO14) carry no entries — their scores roll up from their children. See the
projection rule in frameworks.json.
questionIds is reserved and unused in C1. It exists so a dimension that needs finer
resolution than a pillar can later name specific diagnostic questions without a
schema change. Do not populate it yet.
Every entry carries a rationale. A mapping a consultant cannot defend in a room is
not a mapping.
Sorted by id, code-unit order. Ids are allocation-ordered and never renumbered.

entries.rationale: DMBOK's Data Governance knowledge area is decision rights, stewardship and the council structure — which is what P01 measures directly.
The knowledge area also covers strategy, funding and the governance business case, which DGIW separates into P02.
Enterprise data architecture, the data model landscape and architectural standards are P03's subject.
DMBOK's architecture area also covers the technology landscape the architecture is realised on, which DGIW holds in P10.
Conceptual, logical and physical modelling is architecture work and sits in P03.
Model artefacts are metadata: the definitions and structures a model produces are what P04 asks whether the organisation curates.
Storage, database operations and the platform they run on are P10.
Operations includes retention and disposal execution, which DGIW measures under P09.
A clean one-to-one: DMBOK Data Security and P08 Security & Privacy address the same capability with the same evidence.
Integration is largely pipeline and platform capability, which P10 measures.
Interoperability is where lineage is created or lost; P07 asks whether movement between systems is traceable.
Integration patterns and interface standards are architectural decisions held in P03.
Records management, retention schedules and disposal are the substance of this knowledge area and of P09.
Content management carries classification and access control obligations, measured in P08.
Unstructured content is governed through its metadata — taxonomy and tagging — which is P04.
A clean one-to-one with P06 MDM & Reference Data; no part of this knowledge area falls outside it.
Business intelligence is the consumption end of the data estate, which P11 measures.
The warehouse itself is platform: P10 asks whether the analytical estate is engineered rather than assembled.
Glossary, catalogue and metadata capture are exactly what P04 assesses.
DMBOK treats lineage as a metadata type; DGIW gives lineage its own pillar, so a share of this area lands in P07.
Profiling, rules, measurement and remediation map directly onto P05.

Under BCBS 239 a bank must evidence accuracy through to source, so demonstrating data quality becomes partly a lineage exercise. This does not apply to a sector-neutral engagement, so it is banking-only and DM11 retains 0.85 under core.
Strategy and business case is P02's whole subject; nothing in this component falls elsewhere.
Funding model and programme mandate are strategy questions in P02.
Programme structure, resourcing and who is accountable for delivery is operating-model territory, P01.
Business and data architecture — the model of the business and its data — is P03.
DCAM places the business glossary and the definition of critical data in this component; DGIW measures those in P04.
Identifying the entities the business runs on is master-data work, P06.
Technology architecture is the platform and tooling estate, P10.
The architectural standards governing that estate remain P03.
DCAM expects the technology architecture to make data flow traceable, which is P07.
Data quality management maps directly onto P05.
The same BCBS 239 argument as DM11: evidencing quality to a regulator means evidencing it to source. Banking-only, so DCAM5 retains 0.85 under core.
DCAM's Data Governance component is roles, authority and the governance forum — P01.
It also carries the mandate and its alignment to business objectives, which is P02.
The control environment is largely access, classification and protective controls — P08.
A control with no named owner is not a control; the accountability half sits in P01.

Demonstrating control effectiveness to a regulator requires traceable flow from source to report. Banking-only, so DCAM7 retains 0.75 under core — the largest retained-share gap in this crosswalk and the one most worth showing a client.
Analytics management and P11 AI & Consumption address the same capability.
Mission and vision for data governance is the strategy statement P02 assesses.
Goals, success measures and funding strategy are strategy-level commitments, P02.
Governance metrics are reported into and acted on by the governance forum, which P01 measures.
Data definitions are the glossary; P04 asks whether they exist, are agreed and are used.
DGI's 'data rules' are business rules that become quality rules — the substance of P05.
Rules that constrain structure are architectural standards, P03.
In a bank, the contested definitions are product, GL and counterparty hierarchies — reference data governance, P06. Banking-only, so DGI03 retains 0.90 under core.
Decision rights are P01's defining subject. A clean one-to-one.
Accountabilities map wholly onto P01 — who owns what, and what follows when they do not.
DGI's controls are predominantly protective and access controls, P08.
Data-content controls are quality controls, measured in P05.
Control ownership and the escalation path when a control fails is P01.
Identifying and engaging stakeholders is operating-model work — who sits in the forum and who is consulted.
Stakeholder engagement is also how the mandate is sustained, which P02 assesses.

The DG Office as a structural element of the operating model — its constitution, its place in the forum hierarchy and its decision rights — is P01. This was authored at 1.00 as 'a clean one-to-one'; that was true of the office's EXISTENCE and wrong about the component, which also covers how the office is funded and what it operates. Reduced to 0.60 with the remainder mapped explicitly.
Stewardship as a role — appointment, mandate, time allocation — is P01.
What stewards actually do day to day is triage and remediate quality issues, which P05 measures.
The governance processes themselves — issue escalation, exception handling, change — are P01.
DGI's 'reactive' processes are predominantly data quality issue management, P05.
'Ongoing' processes include retention, archival and disposal cycles, which DGIW measures in P09.
Setting and maintaining the governance framework is the definition of P01.
EDM01 requires the framework to be aligned to enterprise objectives, which is P02.
Benefits delivery is the business case and its realisation — P02.
For a data programme, benefit is overwhelmingly realised at the consumption end, P11.
Data risk in COBIT terms is dominated by security, privacy and regulatory exposure — P08.
Risk appetite is set and monitored by the governance body, P01.
Poor data quality is itself an operational risk that EDM03 expects to be optimised, P05.
BCBS 239 makes risk data aggregation a lineage problem: a bank must show how a risk number was derived. Banking-only, so EDM03 retains 0.80 under core.
Resource optimisation for data is predominantly platform and tooling efficiency, P10.
People are the scarce resource in data governance — steward time allocation is P01.
Resourcing decisions follow from the funding strategy, P02.
Stakeholder engagement and transparency of governance reporting are operating-model capabilities, P01.
EDM05 is also about communicating value and direction to stakeholders, which is P02.
APO14.01 is explicitly the data management strategy — P02.
The same practice defines roles and responsibilities, which is P01.
A consistent business glossary is P04's central artefact. A clean one-to-one.
Metadata management processes are P04.
This practice names infrastructure explicitly — the catalogue tooling — which DGIW holds in P10.
A data quality strategy is P05.
In a regulated bank the quality strategy has to state how accuracy is evidenced to source. Banking-only, so APO14.04 retains 0.85 under core.
Profiling methodology is quality practice, P05.
The practice names tools explicitly; profiling capability is bounded by the platform, P10.
A quality assessment approach maps wholly onto P05.
Cleansing is remediation, the closing half of the quality cycle P05 measures.
In practice most cleansing effort is deduplication and survivorship on master data, P06.
Managing the lifecycle of data assets is P09's subject.
Lifecycle stages have to be designed into the architecture to be enforceable, P03.
Archiving and retention is P09. A clean one-to-one.
Backup and restore is an operational platform capability, P10.
Restore windows are set by retention obligations, which P09 measures.

DGI's DGO component covers the office's mandate and funding strategy, not only its structure. A DG Office that cannot fund itself past the next budget cycle is the failure P02 measures, and nothing else in the DGI crosswalk reaches it.

The DGO is the operator of the catalogue, quality engine and lineage collection. A governance tool at 8% population is a DGO capacity finding that gets misread as a tooling problem, and P10 is where it is actually measured.
